items.stem: Which Ruby construct is best for sharing a set of methods across several unrelated classes?

options.text: A module mixed in with include
options.rationale: Correct: a module mixin injects shared behaviour into any class that includes it.
Inheritance ties classes into one hierarchy, unsuitable for unrelated classes.
Globals share data, not methods, and are discouraged.

options.text: A separate script file with no module
options.rationale: Loading a file alone does not share methods onto classes.

items.explanation: Correct: a module mixin injects shared behaviour into any class that includes it.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about Ruby exception handling are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: rescue can catch a specific error class such as Errno::ENOENT
options.rationale: Correct: you can rescue specific classes to handle known failures.

options.text: An ensure block runs whether or not an exception was raised
options.rationale: Correct: ensure always runs, which suits cleanup.

options.text: rescue without a class should be used to swallow all errors silently
options.rationale: Swallowing every error hides real bugs and is discouraged.

options.text: raise can only be called by the Ruby runtime, not your code
options.rationale: You can raise exceptions explicitly in your own code.

items.explanation: Correct: you can rescue specific classes to handle known failures.; Correct: ensure always runs, which suits cleanup.
